summary: SCI PASS. All eight source prose objects and four unsolved review questions are covered faithfully in both languages. Historical identities, dates, quantities, capacities, rankings, policy and planning/completion distinctions are retained with honest historical attribution. Exact provenance and all 145 bound text files pass before and after; the initial HOLD remains unchanged. paragraphCoverage.concepts: 1920 adoption, the source's first-plan claim, the State Plan for the Electrification of Russia, Lenin as initiator/advocate and his economic judgment. Historical attribution preserved, not presented as a present-day fact or a physical law.

Both necessary conditions in the attributed Lenin quotation retained, including industry, agriculture and transport. English is a translation of the supplied Chinese source, not represented as an independently authenticated original English quotation.

Source's half-century historical assessment; 1913 baseline; industrial production doubled, electricity rose to four times the baseline, not a fourfold increase added to baseline; all targets exceeded after 10 years before deadline; yearly pace growth; 1947 first-in-Europe and second-world rankings kept historical.

Cross-page continuation complete. Nearly five times the whole-1921 electrical energy output in one day is retained as the source's historical comparison, not a power comparison. Source first-year qualifier retained. 我国 correctly resolves contextually to the Soviet Union, not the learner's country.

Approximately 20 percent of electricity generation, not capacity share; Krasnoyarsk historical identity and founding-50-year commemorative name; generating units rated at 500000 kW and total station power six million kW. Source's largest/most-powerful claims explicitly historical; no current capacity or ranking asserted.

Thermal-station development toward greater power; many above one million kW, many above two million kW; Krivorozhsk three million kW and historical largest claim. Power/capacity correctly distinguished from energy output.

Growing nuclear-power role and twenty-fifth CPSU congress resolution prioritizing nuclear development in the European part of the Soviet Union. This is attributed period policy, not today's policy or a universally applicable engineering prescription.

Siberia/Central Asia and European-region power-system interconnection; unified all-Soviet system in formation; reliability/flexibility benefit conditioned on grid and operation; 500000 V, 750000 V and 1150000 V construction requirements retained without claiming all lines were already built.
